title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 11

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the non-conformance lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The quality engineering tutor will review non-conformance reports on Thursday at one. Students should bring the sample report and the relevant specification extract. The class will identify the requirement, the observed result and the evidence needed for review. The tutor will explain why a report should describe the issue precisely without assigning blame.
options: At one on Thursday
At twelve on Thursday
At one on Friday
At two on Thursday

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which extract should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The quality engineering tutor will review non-conformance reports on Thursday at one. Students should bring the sample report and the relevant specification extract. The class will identify the requirement, the observed result and the evidence needed for review. The tutor will explain why a report should describe the issue precisely without assigning blame.
options: The inspection checklist and measurement record
The sample report and specification extract
The audit plan and non-conformance log
The maintenance history and component list

tasks.prompt: A non-conformance report records a failure to meet a stated requirement. It should identify the affected item, the requirement, the observed condition and supporting evidence. The report may also identify immediate containment or a proposed review action, but the cause should not be stated as confirmed unless the investigation supports it. Clear reporting helps the responsible team decide what to examine next. Reading 1. Which information should a non-conformance report identify?
options: Supplier address, purchase value, invoice and delivery time
Staff name, annual leave, shift preference and training date
Affected item, requirement, observed condition and supporting evidence
Equipment colour, storage location, room number and group

tasks.prompt: When may the cause be stated as confirmed?
options: As soon as a possible cause has been suggested
When the reporting form has been completed
When the same symptom has appeared on another item
Only when the investigation supports it

tasks.prompt: The affected item and requirement ___ in the report.
options: must be identified
must identify
identifying
are identify

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO elements of a clear non-conformance report.
options: An unsupported accusation
An unrelated personal comment
Observed condition
Supporting evidence

tasks.prompt: A formal record of a failure to meet a specified requirement is a non-conformance ___.
You have evidence of a non-conformance but no confirmed cause. What should you write?
options: The operator caused the problem.
The observed condition does not meet the stated requirement; the cause remains under investigation.
The cause is obvious, so no evidence is needed.
I will close the report.

tasks.prompt: Arrange the steps for documenting a requirement failure and its supporting evidence.
options: Attach or reference supporting evidence
Identify the affected item and requirement
Record the issue for review without assuming a cause
Describe the observed condition
correctOrder: Identify the affected item and requirement
Record the issue for review without assuming a cause

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining how to prepare a non-conformance report. Include the requirement, observed condition, evidence and the distinction between a finding and its cause.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Report content — 2: identifies the requirement, observed condition and relevant evidence; 1: includes some; 0: absent. (2) Finding versus cause — 2: clearly distinguishes the observed non-conformance from a cause that may remain unconfirmed; 1: partial; 0: conflates them. (3) Objectivity and structure — 2: proposes factual, traceable wording without unsupported assumptions; 1: partly objective; 0: speculative or unclear. (4) English — 2: precise technical vocabulary and coherent 100–120-word response; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
